name: MonarchFavicon
title: Favicon
summary: The icon of a website at a fixed size, with a letter tile while it loads, when it fails and when there is no icon.
whenToUse: Beside the name or address of a website, in link lists, bookmarks and source citations.
whenNotToUse: For a person or an organisation use the avatar. For an app's own symbols use MonarchIcon.
api: init(image: Image?, name: String, label: String? = nil, size: MonarchFaviconSize = .sm, shape: MonarchFaviconShape = .rounded)
init(url: URL?, name: String, label: String? = nil, size: MonarchFaviconSize = .sm, shape: MonarchFaviconShape = .rounded)
enum MonarchFaviconSize { case sm, md, lg }
enum MonarchFaviconShape { case rounded, circle, square }

options.name: image
options.description: An icon the app already has, or nil for the letter tile. First initialiser.

options.name: url
options.description: The address of the icon, loaded with AsyncImage. Only http and https URLs are loaded. Second initialiser.

options.name: name
options.description: The name of the site, its domain or its URL. Its first letter or digit is the fallback letter.

options.name: label
options.description: What VoiceOver reads. Without it the favicon is decorative.

options.name: size
options.description: sm 16, md 20 or lg 24 points, before Dynamic Type.

states.name: image
states.description: The picture fills the tile and is clipped to the shape.

states.name: fallback
states.description: A tile in the muted background colour with one upper-case letter in the muted text colour. Shown while loading, on failure and without a source.

appearance: The picture is drawn as it is. The letter tile uses the muted background and muted text roles, which resolve per theme, including high contrast.
platformNotes: The web Favicon takes a domain and an optional resolveSrc function, and a size in pixels. iOS follows the Monarch image convention instead: one initialiser with an Image and one with a URL, and three named sizes. Like the web, Monarch never calls a favicon service by itself. The web also accepts base64 data URLs; on iOS an app with image data passes an Image.
accessibility: Decorative and hidden from VoiceOver unless label is given.
With a label it is one element with the image trait, read as the label.
The tile and the letter scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A URL with a scheme other than http or https, or without a host, is not loaded and the letter tile is shown.
A name with no letter or digit gives a question mark.
A name that is a URL or starts with www. is reduced to its host name before the letter is taken.
AsyncImage does not cache beyond the shared URL cache; an app with its own image pipeline passes an Image.
The letter is sized as 0.6 of the tile rather than with a type role, so it fits every size.

examples.title: Letter fallbacks in a list
An icon the app already has
examples.code: MonarchFavicon(image: Image(systemName: "globe"), name: "Globe", label: "Globe", size: .lg, shape: .circle)
